thread:
Priya: Noticed a NIC tx-queue saturation on eu-west rack-9 this morning. One tenant's large embedding batch overloaded the link and caused packet drops + nearby pods to balloon GPU mem and trigger soft preempts.
Leo: Which tenant is it?
Priya: @analytics-squad. They pushed a 4k embedding batch across 12 pods; each pod peaked ~600Mbps egress for ~15m. Router counters show a coordinated spike.
Anita: That matches the cluster-wide slice_eviction blip we saw. Did rack shaping fire?
Priya: No. Our shaping is per-node NIC class; we don't enforce per-tenant shaping inside the node. So a single tenant can fill the kernel tx queue and starve others.
Maya: Short-term mitigation ideas? Proxy-level throttling per-tenant token bucket?
Oliver: Proxy throttles help but are reactive and increase the throttled tenant's tail latency. I'm proposing infra-level per-tenant egress shaping using eBPF cgroup classifiers (low overhead) + an automated soft quarantine that routes noisy tenants to a fractional dedicated slice for heavy batch windows.
Kai: Sounds reasonable. Do you have an example rule?
Oliver: Prototype snippet: ```# eBPF tenant egress map
map tenant_rate: key=tenant_id value=bytes_per_sec
if tenant_rate > 400mbps -> mark_noisy
action: tc qdisc tbf rate 200mbit burst 32k latency 50ms
```
Priya: Once marked noisy, scheduler can route new allocations for that tenant to a fractional-slice with isolated egress lanes to avoid collateral on shared slices.
Leo: We need a quick cost/benefit calc. Fractional slices reduce packing efficiency.
Kai: Back-of-envelope: analytics-squad incident produced ~1.62TB egress peak yesterday on that rack, causing ~7 slot-hours of delay and ~ $1.2k extra infra impact. If we put them on a fractional slice we may double their dedicated cost but avoid 10x collateral cost for others. Net neutral or slightly better.
Maya: Proposed test plan: 1) apply eBPF rule on a single canary node; 2) emit mark_noisy metric; 3) route mark_noisy tenants to fractional-slice-proxy with 3% traffic split; 4) monitor nic_tx_queue_drop, p99_token_latency, slice_eviction_count for 4 hours.
deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: tenant-egress-ebpf v0.2 -> nodes=[eu-west-b-09] by @oliver. Watchlist: nic_tx_queue_drop, kvcache_miss, scheduler.preempt_events.
Priya: I'll reach out to Sales to advise analytics-squad on batch windows and offer fractional reserved slices as opt-in. Also suggest we add a tenant_egress_mark metric into billing logs so we can correlate noisy events to invoices.
Oliver: One more follow-up: consider adding a kernel-level nic tx-queue probe that exports per-cgroup queue length so eBPF decision logic can react earlier (pre-drops). Low effort and high signal.
Leo: Agree. Let's run the canary this afternoon. :thumbsup:
